notes: 217 pieces, matching the parts list type by type, colour by colour. The minifigure parts (helmet, visor, head, torso, legs) are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.

The booklet builds TWO separate models, so two separate groups are correct and I kept them. The first is the small fan display stand on pages 5-10, steps 1-10 (b1-b23). The second is the McLaren Senna car from page 11 on (b24-b217). The car's step numbering restarts at 1 on page 11, it has its own preview picture, and the stand is never joined to the car.

The car is built from sub-assemblies that are all joined into one group: car body (b24-b76), front end (b77-b161, folded onto the car at step 32), rear wing (b162-b175), rear end (b176-b199) and four wheels (b200-b215). The wrench (b216) and sticker sheet (b217) are loose pieces. I linked them to the car by joins: the wrench is shown beside the wheel on page 61, and the stickers go on car parts such as b163.

b17 (propeller) does not rest on the round tile b13, because a tile has no studs. It is held only by the axle pin b18, so its rests_on is empty. b136 and b137 (29119) rest on the orange wedge plates b111/b112, which have studs, not on the 3070b tiles.

Where the isometric drawings are ambiguous, which pieces a part rests on is my best reading. This applies especially to the front end and the pieces that attach sideways. Pieces that attach to side studs or are clipped on are recorded in other_joins and have empty rests_on. Pieces that clutch nothing below them also have empty rests_on.
Orange wheels and tyres are recorded as friction fits with empty rests_on. Each axle pin goes through a pin-hole of an 18975 brick: b99 for the front wheels and b48 for the rear wheels.
Stickers are not separate parts and are not recorded.
